skills.name: teach
skills.purpose: Stateful 'teach me anything' tutor: grounds learning in a MISSION.md, gathers trusted resources, then produces short self-contained HTML lessons in the learner's zone of proximal development with retrieval practice, spacing, interleaving, quizzes and learning records across sessions.
skills.how_to_use: User-invoked only (`/teach <topic>`, disable-model-invocation). Treats the current folder as a teaching workspace (MISSION.md, RESOURCES.md, lessons/*.html, learning-records/, assets/); uses web search for sources. No API keys.
skills.evidence: skills.sh ~747.5k installs (top 'teach' result; repo-wide installs inflate this somewhat); Matt Pocock's skills repo (275k stars); copied into vinvcn/mattpocock-skills-zh-cn (~4.8k installs)
skills.notes: Learner-facing tutor; strong learning-science core (fluency vs storage strength, desirable difficulty, equal-length quiz options so formatting gives no clues).

skills.name: k12-lesson-plan-creation
skills.purpose: Builds a classroom-ready, standards-aligned K-12 lesson (math, ELA, science, social studies) with subject-specific pedagogy: lesson plan, student-facing materials and a teacher observation template, rendered as editable Word documents from one material-source JSON.
skills.how_to_use: Triggers on lesson/mini-lesson/unit-plan requests or implicit teacher intent ('teaching long division to 5th graders tomorrow'). Install the plugin from anthropics/k12-teacher-skills; bundled Python scripts render .docx (pip-installs python-docx). Uses the Learning Commons Knowledge Graph connector for standards when connected, works without it.
skills.evidence: Official Anthropic, co-developed with Learning Commons, ships with eval rubrics; skills.sh ~82 installs (+15 via learning-commons-org/agent-skills mirror); listed on mcpservers.org, ClaudeMap, awesomeclaudeplugins; aiskill.market write-ups
skills.notes: Skill folder has its own Apache-2.0 LICENSE. The plugin's .mcp.json also wires optional vendor connectors (ASSISTments, Brisk, Canva, Coteach, Diffit, Eedi, MagicSchool, Snorkl, TeachFX) at their official endpoints; the skill works without them.

skills.name: k12-check-for-understanding
skills.purpose: Writes a 1-3 item formative Check for Understanding for a math topic or standard, with distractors drawn from documented student misconceptions and a teacher guide that routes each likely response to a specific next instructional step.
skills.how_to_use: Triggers on 'check for understanding', 'exit ticket', 'quick check' or 'I need to see who got it before I move on' (math only). Same plugin as k12-lesson-plan-creation; Learning Commons Knowledge Graph optional.
skills.evidence: Official Anthropic + Learning Commons with eval rubrics; skills.sh ~48 installs (+14 via mirror)
skills.notes: Best public example of misconception-based distractor writing. Folder has LICENSE and NOTICE (Apache-2.0).

skills.name: k12-lesson-differentiation
skills.purpose: Adapts an existing K-12 lesson into below/at/above-proficiency tiers (Tomlinson framework plus subject-specific access design): one teacher differentiation plan and three student-ready tier documents written from one shared source so tiers cannot drift.
skills.how_to_use: Triggers on 'differentiate / tier / scaffold this lesson' or 'my students are at different levels'; the teacher brings or names the lesson. Same plugin and render scripts as k12-lesson-plan-creation.
skills.evidence: Official Anthropic + Learning Commons; skills.sh ~135 installs (+35 via mirror); ProSkillsMD candidate listing
skills.notes: Covers scaffolding and inclusive access. Sibling skill k12-lesson-prep (a short lesson-internalisation prep partner) lives in the same plugin.

skills.name: mentoring-juniors
skills.purpose: Socratic mentor for junior developers and AI newcomers: guides through questions and progressive clues instead of giving answers, with a 5-phase response protocol (context, questioning, concept, clues, validation) and a delivery-vs-learning balance for urgent work.
skills.how_to_use: Triggers on 'help me understand', 'teach me', 'I'm stuck', 'mentor me', 'what does this error mean'. No prerequisites.
skills.evidence: GitHub's official awesome-copilot collection (39.7k stars); skills.sh ~7.0k installs; featured on skillsmp.com 'teaching' search
skills.notes: Written for Copilot (mentions Copilot tools and a PEAR loop) and for coding; the Socratic method transfers to any subject.

skills.name: codebase-to-course
skills.purpose: Turns any codebase into an interactive single-page HTML course for non-technical learners: scroll-based modules, animated visualisations, embedded quizzes and code shown beside plain-English translations.
skills.how_to_use: Triggers on 'turn this into a course', 'teach this code', 'interactive tutorial from code'; point it at a local folder, the current project or a GitHub URL (it clones to /tmp). Output opens in a browser with no setup.
skills.evidence: 5.6k stars; in hesreallyhim/awesome-claude-code; many copies on skills.sh (devenkhatri, practicalswan, cedricmatalog forks)
skills.notes: No licence file in the repo: link-only. Only external dependency of the generated course is the Google Fonts CDN.

skills.name: backwards-design-unit-planner
skills.purpose: Plans a unit with Understanding by Design: desired outcomes, then assessment evidence, then learning activities, with constructive alignment (Wiggins & McTighe, Biggs & Tang) and typed inputs/outputs for chaining.
skills.how_to_use: Use when starting or redesigning a unit; give desired outcomes, student level and unit length. Install the whole library as a plugin (`claude plugin install https://github.com/GarethManning/education-agent-skills`) or copy the folder.
skills.evidence: Largest education skill library (165 evidence-cited skills); listed in Anthropic's claude-plugins-community marketplace (claude-education-skills-library); several skills in VoltAgent/awesome-agent-skills; skills.sh ~163 installs
skills.notes: GitHub shows NOASSERTION but LICENSE is CC BY-SA 4.0: ShareAlike means any distilled guide built from it must also be CC BY-SA with attribution. Same library has criterion-referenced-rubric-generator, assessment-validity-checker, scope-and-sequence-designer, worked-example-fading-designer and cognitive-load-analyser. Optional hosted MCP (author's Vercel endpoint) needs a token; local use sends nothing.

skills.name: book-study
skills.purpose: Reading coach that takes a learner through a book chapter by chapter: pre-reading guide, knowledge compilation, mastery tests with a required practice phase, a mastery map and spaced-repetition reviews with expanding intervals.
skills.how_to_use: Triggers on 'read this book with me', 'quiz me on the book', 'review what I read' or `/book-study` with sub-commands ingest, query, review, compare, status. No prerequisites.
skills.evidence: skills.sh ~3.2k installs; repo 3.9k stars
skills.notes: Learner-facing; good worked pattern for mastery checks plus spaced review.

skills.name: flashcards
skills.purpose: Generates flashcards from the learner's own outline or notes and drills them with Leitner buckets, self-assessment, due-card prioritisation, stats and focused N-card sessions; flags cards made without a source with [VERIFY].
skills.how_to_use: `/flashcards [subject] --generate | --drill | --review | --stats | --session <n>`; part of the law-student plugin in anthropics/claude-for-legal. Stores decks under ~/.claude/plugins/config/claude-for-legal/law-student/flashcards/.
skills.evidence: Official Anthropic (Claude for Legal); skills.sh ~730 installs
skills.notes: Framed for law school (black-letter rules, real-matter check) but the card-writing and Leitner drill logic is general. Says itself it is not a full SRS ('if you want Anki, use Anki'). Sibling socratic-drill skill in the same plugin does ask-and-push-back Socratic drilling.

skills.name: openmaic
skills.purpose: Sets up and drives OpenMAIC, an open multi-agent interactive classroom generator: turns a topic or uploaded PDF into a classroom with slides, narration, AI teacher/classmate agents, quizzes and interactive widgets, and guides extending its SDK.
skills.how_to_use: Triggers on 'generate an interactive classroom' or OpenMAIC setup. Either the hosted Live Demo (access code from open.maic.chat) or a self-hosted instance with your own LLM provider keys in openmaic.yml; confirmation-heavy, one phase at a time.
skills.evidence: Tsinghua MAIC project; repo created Mar 2026 and already ~39.9k stars; skills.sh ~255 installs; new DeepSeek variant THU-MAIC/dsh-openmaic (Aug 2026)
skills.notes: Live Demo mode uploads materials to open.maic.chat (the project's own hosted service); self-hosting keeps data local. The repo's agent-runtime skills (understanding-by-design, zone-of-proximal-development, lecture-style, workshop-style, curriculum-planner, spiral-curriculum) hold good pedagogy but call OpenMAIC runtime tools and are mostly in Chinese.

skills.name: gws-classroom
skills.purpose: Manages Google Classroom through the Workspace CLI: courses, rosters (students/teachers), coursework, materials, announcements, topics, invitations and grading-period settings.
skills.how_to_use: Needs the `gws` CLI installed and Google OAuth (read gws-shared first); companion recipe skill `recipe-create-classroom-course` sets up a course end to end.
skills.evidence: Official Google Workspace CLI; skills.sh ~28.4k installs (recipe-create-classroom-course ~28.3k); in VoltAgent/awesome-agent-skills
skills.notes: Auto-generated API reference rather than pedagogy: the LMS-operations route for Google Classroom.

skills.name: retrieval-practice-generator
skills.purpose: Generates retrieval-practice questions at varied difficulty for a concept (quiz starters, revision, low-stakes testing), grounded in testing-effect research (Roediger & Butler, Karpicke, Agarwal, Dunlosky).
skills.how_to_use: Give topic, student level and question count (6-10 recommended); optional time since learning and student profiles. Same library and install route as backwards-design-unit-planner.
skills.evidence: skills.sh ~149 installs; Anthropic community marketplace listing; VoltAgent list
skills.notes: CC BY-SA 4.0 (ShareAlike). Pair with spaced-practice-scheduler and interleaving-unit-planner from the same memory-learning-science domain.

skills.name: tutor
skills.purpose: Quiz-based tutor that tracks what a learner knows at concept level: diagnostic assessment, section study, drills on weak areas and a progress dashboard, over an Obsidian StudyVault.
skills.how_to_use: Run tutor-setup first to turn PDFs, web pages or a codebase into a StudyVault, then '/tutor', 'quiz me', 'test me'. Also triggers in Korean.
skills.evidence: skills.sh ~2.3k installs; in VoltAgent/awesome-agent-skills
skills.notes: Learner-facing; useful pattern for concept-level mastery tracking.

skills.name: eli5
skills.purpose: Explains any topic, code, concept or error at the right level for a named audience (child, manager, new hire, expert), choosing vocabulary, analogies and depth to match.
skills.how_to_use: Triggers on 'ELI5', 'explain this to my...', 'dumb it down', 'break this down for'. No prerequisites.
skills.evidence: skills.sh ~1.4k installs; 1.6k stars
skills.notes: Covers the explanations/analogies part of the craft; single SKILL.md.

skills.name: udl-lesson-auditor
skills.purpose: Audits an existing lesson against Universal Design for Learning (engagement, representation, action/expression), names concrete access barriers and ranks modifications by impact.
skills.how_to_use: Give the lesson plan and learner context (age, EAL learners, IEPs, reading range); optional constraints. Same library and install route as backwards-design-unit-planner.
skills.evidence: Cites CAST UDL Guidelines 2.2 and Rose & Meyer; library listed in Anthropic community marketplace and VoltAgent
skills.notes: CC BY-SA 4.0 (ShareAlike). Covers accessibility and inclusive teaching; siblings udl-barrier-anticipator and udl-options-designer.

skills.name: learn-from-materials
skills.purpose: Turns books, PDFs, slides, documents and web pages into a source-grounded knowledge base plus interactive learning pages (explanations, quizzes, relationship maps) in English or Chinese, separating material facts, inference and external checks.
skills.how_to_use: Triggers on learning, summarising, reviewing or quizzing on supplied materials. Needs Python 3.10+; Node/Playwright optional for browser checks; OCR helps with scanned PDFs. A fixed renderer builds the HTML from JSON (no hand-written HTML).
skills.evidence: Repo created 8 Sep 2026 and at ~786 stars within four weeks; in VoltAgent/awesome-agent-skills
skills.notes: LICENSE.md and NOTICE.md credit MIT upstreams (virgiliojr94/book-to-skill and book-to-webpage). Generated pages make no network calls and collect no keys or telemetry.

skills.name: universal-diagnostic-tutor
skills.purpose: Diagnosis-first tutor (strongest on university STEM, AI/CS) that maps subject, prerequisites and likely knowledge gaps before teaching, then runs practice, answer checking, mistake review, mastery checks, study plans and cross-chat state cards.
skills.how_to_use: Natural-language intents (teach me, practice, grade my answer, study plan, exam drill), English or Chinese; legacy /tutor, /practice, /diagnose-gap text recognised. Ships curated source packs (MIT OCW, Stanford, OpenStax, d2l.ai).
skills.evidence: Repo created 26 Jun 2026, ~236 stars; top-starred new tutor repo in gh search (created after 1 Jun 2026)
skills.notes: Explicitly refuses answer-first homework-bot behaviour, cheating and exam leaks.

skills.name: learning-objectives
skills.purpose: Evidence-based learning-objective development: writes intended learning outcomes, classifies them on the revised Bloom's taxonomy, builds a bidirectional alignment matrix with assessments and flags expertise-reversal risks.
skills.how_to_use: Part of the idstack instructional-design pipeline (`/idstack:pipeline` chains needs-analysis -> learning-objectives -> assessment-design -> course-builder -> course-quality-review -> course-export); reads and extends the .idstack project manifest. Install via the repo's Claude Code plugin marketplace.
skills.evidence: Listed in Anthropic's claude-plugins-community marketplace ('evidence-based instructional design pipeline, 11 skills'); ~1,200-line skill with peer-reviewed references; low stars
skills.notes: Most complete ADDIE-style instructional design pipeline found. No telemetry per PRIVACY.md; optional Consensus API lookups (api.consensus.app, the vendor's own API, only with your own key) and an hourly git fetch update check against GitHub.

skills.name: course-export
skills.purpose: Exports a built course to an LMS: IMS Common Cartridge (.imscc) for Canvas, Blackboard, Moodle and D2L, a SCORM package, or a direct push of modules, pages, assignments and discussions to Canvas via its REST API.
skills.how_to_use: Last stage of the idstack pipeline (reads course-builder output and the manifest). Cartridge/SCORM need no credentials; Canvas push needs your institution's Canvas access token and confirmation of the target course. Sibling course-import reads .imscc, SCORM 1.2/2004 or Canvas API.
skills.evidence: Only substantive public skill found for SCORM / IMS Common Cartridge / Canvas export; Anthropic community marketplace listing
skills.notes: Canvas calls go only to the Canvas instance you name, with your token (not stored). Same opt-in Consensus and update-check notes as learning-objectives.

skills.name: assessment-architect
skills.purpose: Builds assessment instruments for university courses: test blueprints, exam/quiz/question-bank item writing, analytic/holistic/single-point rubrics, TILT project briefs, AI-era integrity audits, verified answer keys and post-exam item analysis.
skills.how_to_use: Triggers on exam, quiz, rubric, question bank, item analysis (English or Chinese); stage 3 of the teaching-skills pipeline (course-designer -> lesson-builder -> assessment-architect -> ...). References include rubric patterns, grade analysis and LMS export formats.
skills.evidence: 15-skill teaching-lifecycle suite for university professors, active (pushed Oct 2026); skills.sh ~10 installs; found via web search and gh search; low stars
skills.notes: Strongest item-writing and item-analysis coverage found. Siblings: course-designer (Bloom-tagged outcomes, syllabus, constructive alignment), lesson-builder, media-scripter (lesson video scripts), deck-studio, student-mentor.
